mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to a tightening monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent monetary tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over the previous 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE decrease > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous 3 months signals increased economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase > 5% does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the previous 3 months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decrease > 2% does not correlate with subsequent economic contraction.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal: low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 1%, or FEDFUNDS < 1% does not correlate with subsequent positive equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal: when both real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 1% over the previous 3 months, it signals robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and PAYEMS increase > 1% in 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint increase in RSAFS and PAYEMS does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal: during a late-cycle expansion, a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% over the previous 3 months signals tightening labor markets, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE decrease > 0.3% does not correlate with subsequent economic growth during late-cycle expansions.

mechanism_narrative: A threshold-triggered signal: when industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 3% over the previous 3 months, it signals strong supply-side growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 3% does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.
